sources.entry: OpenTripPlanner - Multimodal trip planning software based on OpenStreetMap data and consuming published GTFS-formatted data to suggest routes using local public transit systems. (Source Code) LGPL-3.0 Java/Javascript

summary.one_liner: OpenTripPlanner is an open source multimodal trip planner that builds routes from GTFS transit data and OpenStreetMap, with real-time updates and GraphQL APIs.
summary.what_it_does: OpenTripPlanner (OTP) is a multi-modal trip planner focused on scheduled public transportation combined with bicycling, walking, bike share, and ride hailing. Its server runs on any platform with a Java virtual machine. It builds its transportation network from open data, primarily GTFS and OpenStreetMap. It applies real-time updates and alerts so itineraries account for disruptions and service changes. It exposes GraphQL APIs that clients such as open source JavaScript components and native mobile apps can use. The repository also includes a JavaScript test client based on MapLibre, and the Maven build produces a single shaded JAR file. This branch is OpenTripPlanner 2, the only major version still supported.
use_cases: Plan multimodal trips combining public transit, biking, and walking
Build a transit trip planner app or website on GTFS data
Route around real-time transit delays and service alerts
Provide GraphQL trip planning API for mobile or web clients
Integrate bike share and ride hailing into itinerary suggestions
how_to_run: Build the project with Maven to produce otp-shaded/target/otp-shaded-VERSION.jar
Run the shaded JAR with Java to start the OpenTripPlanner server
See the main documentation for a quick introduction and setup instructions
notable: Consumes open standard transit data (GTFS and OpenStreetMap) rather than proprietary feeds
Applies real-time transit updates so routing accounts for disruptions
Exposes GraphQL APIs for multiple client types
Performance speed test runs on every merged PR and is published as a dashboard
Originally launched by TriMet, Portland's transport agency, in 2009
caveats: Server requires a Java virtual machine and a Maven build to run from source
The included JavaScript client is mainly for testing; most deployments build custom clients
keywords: plan a trip by bus and bike
